key_insight: The sign of a sizable second Josephson harmonic guides two superconducting qutrit designs that strongly suppress relaxation but remain limited by dephasing.
engineering_relevance: Three-junction loops could encode three-level quantum states with hardware-level noise protection, with the preferred design depending on material properties and dominant noise sources.
method: Use a positive second harmonic and slight junction asymmetry to create a tunable, symmetry-protected qutrit.
Use a negative second harmonic with weak symmetry breaking, such as a Josephson diode effect, to realize an alternative protected qutrit.
Microscopically model altermagnetic junctions to assess gate-controlled selection of the second-harmonic sign.
evidence_signal: Theoretical analysis identifies complementary noise-protection trade-offs, while microscopic calculations show gate-controlled harmonic sign selection; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Both designs require a sizable second harmonic, and gate-voltage noise becomes the leading dephasing source in the modeled gate-tunable platform.
paper_title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
